== Research Notes ==
=== Children in the Miami Valley memoir ===

The memoir names six children of William B. and Maria H. McIntire: Mary Jane, wife of J. J. Kane (a candidate for [[Glasgow-874|Nancy Jane Kane]]); [[Glasgow-2039|Dr Joseph Anderson]]; Robert, deceased; [[Glasgow-2041|Mary Elizabeth Williams]]; William Arthur, who died at twenty-two; and [[Glasgow-2043|S. S. Glasgow]].<ref name="Miami1919" /> Robert and William Arthur have no confirmed existing-profile destination in the bounded local review; complete evidence drafts remain on HOLD. The mother’s 1859 death differs from the attached [[McIntyre-4103|Marion McIntyre]] account’s 1855 death. Do not resolve those identities or dates by assumption.

The same memoir describes William as a lifelong Adams County farmer, an opponent of slavery and a participant in the Underground Railway. These are the published biographer’s claims; no separate contemporary activity record was inspected. His reported age at death, ninety-one, fits the 1816–1907 account.<ref name="Miami1919" />


=== Father identification ===

[[Glasgow-653|Joseph Glasgow]] is confidently inferred to be this person’s father, assessed 95%. [[Glasgow-875|William Barclay]]’s family is identified by [[Glasgow-2043|Samuel Steele]]’s exact birthday, [[Glasgow-2039|Joseph Anderson]] and [[Glasgow-2041|Mary Elizabeth/Williams]], the Kane daughter, his McIntire wife, Adams County farming and survival to 91. Robert A.’s place beside this William B. connects that specific adult to the Joseph/Nancy family. The remaining alternative is that the memoir mixed paternal as well as maternal sibling groups. <ref name="Miami1919">John C. Hover et al., eds., ''Memoirs of the Miami Valley'' (Robert O. Law Company, 1919–1920), “S. S. Glasgow,” printed pp. 257–258; [https://digital.cincinnatilibrary.org/iiif/2/p16998coll15:18001/full/full/0/default.jpg original p. 257] and [https://digital.cincinnatilibrary.org/iiif/2/p16998coll15:18002/full/full/0/default.jpg original p. 258], Cincinnati & Hamilton County Public Library Digital Library; images inspected 22 October 2026. Published family biography, not a civil or parish register.</ref>

The memoir never names Joseph: its sibling group is linked to [[Glasgow-1625|Robert Anderson]], whose 1880 county biography names Joseph and Nancy. The memoir’s ancestral migration story is inconsistent with Joseph’s Virginia birth, and Eliza/Breckenridge appears to be a Campbell half-sister. These problems qualify the whole-pair inference; no mother or vital fact is changed. The 1880 statement is used from its published citation and held biographical account, not a newly inspected image.


=== Earlier father assessment, 22 October 2026 — superseded ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-653]] is assessed at 71% (probable). William Barclay’s exact 1816 birth fits Joseph-653’s 1780 generation and the established Adams County family. The existing assignment is a specific descendant-family placement, but his retained cemetery, residence and later-life citations do not themselves name Joseph as father.

Probable71%; compiled pedigree with compatible household, not a father proved by a gravestone date.

Next useful test: Read William’s Faris entry and its family-record source.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-875 WikiTree profile export for Glasgow-875]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.
